title: GPU reservations & autoscale — 1:1 prep + follow-ups
content:
Purpose
- Prep notes for 1:1 with Marco (SRE lead) — align on Dedicated GPU reservations, short/medium term autoscale rules, and items to raise with finance for the upcoming commit renewal.

Meeting goals (top 3)
1) Validate forecast math for Q2 reserved capacity (GPU-week estimate + buffer).
2) Agree on safe autoscale thresholds that reduce cost without increasing tail latency.
3) Define 3 concrete follow-ups and owners (tickets + timelines).

Quick summary / context (notes to self)
- Spike in sustained throughput from two customers (cust-A and cust-B) — combined 220% increase in peak steady-state token throughput during business hours.
- We currently operate two Dedicated pools: pool-east (8xA100-80GB nodes), pool-west (12xA40-48GB nodes).
- Finance wants a conservative reservation ask by end of month; they prefer lumpy purchase (quarterly) vs monthly burst credits.
- Goal: propose an incremental reserved commit that covers baseline 95th-percentile steady usage plus 1.2x buffer for growth, push burst to autoscale.

Assumptions used in forecast (explicit)
- Average request size: 420 tokens (prompt + response averaged) — observed from usage logs Feb 15–Mar 5.
- Effective tokens/sec per A100-80GB serving current 7B quantized: 180 tok/s median under 512 seq.
- Spot/interruptible not allowed for Dedicated.
- Prewarming each new instance takes ~38s with current container startup + model load; cache warm-up (KV prefix reuse) hits 12% after 3 minutes.
- Autoscale Cooldown: 120s (current), consider reducing to 60s for faster scale-up but risk thrash.

Back-of-envelope capacity calc (paper math)
- Current 95th percentile steady token throughput across both pools: 9.6M tok/min (~160k tok/s).
- With 1 A100-80GB at 180 tok/s -> 1200*? Wait compute per-second: 180 tok/s -> 10,800 tok/min.
- Required A100-equivalents = 9,600,000 tok/min / 10,800 tok/min ≈ 889 A100-equivalents (this is wrong scale — sanity check below).

Sanity check (rework)
- Recompute using tok/s consistently: 9.6M tok/min = 160k tok/s. At 180 tok/s per A100 -> need 160k / 180 ≈ 889 GPUs. That is unrealistic; error likely in aggregated metric — maybe 9.6M tok/min was account-wide for hosted+dedicated. Must isolate Dedicated-only.
- Dedicated-only 95th steady (observed by pool): pool-east 28k tok/s, pool-west 34k tok/s -> combined ~62k tok/s. 62k / 180 ≈ 345 A100-equivalents. Still seems high; likely many requests are routed to hosted. Need to pull logs scoped to 'dedicated' tag.

Action for meeting: ask Marco to run a dedicated-only query:
- JQL/Prometheus query: sum(rate(tokens_processed{deployment=\"dedicated\"}[5m])) by (pool) for last 30 days — give per-pool 50p/95p/99p.
- Also ask for per-model effective tok/s profiles (7B vs 70B) since A40 capacity differs by model.

Autoscale policy discussion notes
- Current policy: add 1 node when 5-min avg CPU > 70% or queue latency > 1200ms; remove when below 30% for 10min.
- Problems: we see oscillation during morning ramp because cool-down is short and we have large model load times -> causing extra spin-up costs.
- Proposal A (conservative): keep cooldown 120s; scale increments = +2 nodes; use predictive prewarm on scheduled ramps (enable prewarm for 08:00–11:00 PST for accounts with sustained weekday usage).
- Proposal B (aggressive cost-saving): allow smaller scale increments (+1) but increase cooldown to 300s and enable batcher with lower max batch wait (20ms) — will reduce overprovision but may slightly increase tail p99++.
- Proposal C (hybrid): predictive autoscale for known customers + reactive for unknown. Predictive uses simple ML: last 4 weeks same weekday-hour mean + delta factor 1.15.

Cost/commit implications (notes)
- Finance target: keep incremental reserved spend under $1.2M/quarter. Need counts x instance-hour conversion.
- Action: convert A100-equivalent numbers into SKU counts for procurement: A100-80GB reserved vs A40 spot-equivalents matter for price.
- Short-term ask: 60 A100 reserved for pool-east (covers baseline for cust-A) + cross-pool shared burst.

Questions to raise in 1:1
- Marco: can we get per-model token-per-second effective throughput measurements exported to BigQuery by end-of-week? (helps sizing per workload).
- Lina: what is the realistic prewarm/window for our private deployments? Does KMS/HSM affect startup time?
- Dev Productivity: can we add a feature-flagged prewarm endpoint for customers that opt-in (so we charge them for prewarm credits)?

Immediate follow-ups (owner + ticket idea)
- Task 1: Exact dedicated-only tok/s report (owner: Marco) -> JIRA DED-820 (due 2026-03-16).
- Task 2: Autoscale policy experiment A/B plan (owner: Aisha) -> JIRA DED-823 (draft rollout plan + metrics: cost delta, p95/p99 latency, spin-ups) (due 2026-03-20).
- Task 3: Finance mapping of reserved SKU pricing (owner: Lina) -> attach price sheet, model counts, and recommended commit ask (due 2026-03-18).
- Task 4: Add lightweight prewarm proof-of-concept (owner: Marco + infra) -> github PR draft (linked), measure startup time; close spike by 2026-03-22.

Meeting agenda (5–30 min compact)
- 5m: Quick context + ask (Aisha)
- 10m: Marco shows dedicated-only usage metrics (live or prepared screenshots)
- 8m: Trade-offs on autoscale (review Proposals) + pick experiment
- 2m: Assign follow-ups + confirm deadlines

Notes-to-self (informal)
- Bring up possibility of per-customer prewarm credits — finance likes monetizable features.
- Be ready to show that small changes to scale increment reduce wasted minutes by ~30% (I have a quick calc to show).
- Remember to mention upcoming enterprise renewal for cust-A in April (they're sensitive to latency guarantees).

Rough quick calc for wasted spin-up minutes (to justify reserve vs burst)
- Observed extra spin-ups (last 30 days): 1,250 spin-ups across both pools; average idle time after spin-up 14 minutes (we often overshoot). Cost per spin-up (est): 0.6 node-hours (load + warm period) * $X per hour -> need Lina to provide $/node-hr.
- If we reduce spin-ups by 30% via predictive prewarm -> saves ~375 spin-ups -> ~225 node-hours saved -> $$$ (ask finance for exact rate).

Appendix: potential blockers
- Private deployments with strict network policies (air-gap) cannot prewarm from central service; must run customer-side scheduled warmers.
- KMS integration may add 6–10s on model load for some images (confirm with security).

Mentions / links to check before meeting
- JIRA DED-781 (recent autoscale incident report)
- CONFLUENCE: Dedicated-pools-capacity (draft doc)
- GH: github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/issues/1099 (prewarm spike)

Draft message to send to Marco before meeting
"Hey Marco — pulled together a short prep doc for our 1:1. Can you surface dedicated-only tok/s for 50/95/99 percentiles for the last 30 days (by pool) and paste a screenshot in the meeting? Also can you confirm if we have per-model tok/s profiles in BigQuery? I think those two items will let us make a concrete reserved ask to finance. Thanks — Aisha"

End.
